enum.name: FIRMWARE_VERSION_TYPE
enum.description: These values define the type of firmware release. These values indicate the first version or release of this type. For example the first alpha release would be 64, the second would be 65.

enum.name: HL_FAILURE_FLAG
enum.description: Flags to report failure cases over the high latency telemetry.

entry.name: HL_FAILURE_FLAG_ESTIMATOR
entry.description: Estimator failure, for example measurement rejection or large variances.

enum.name: MAV_GOTO
enum.description: Actions that may be specified in MAV_CMD_OVERRIDE_GOTO to override mission execution.

entry.name: MAV_GOTO_DO_CONTINUE
entry.description: Continue with the next item in mission execution.

entry.name: MAV_GOTO_HOLD_AT_CURRENT_POSITION
entry.description: Hold at the current position of the system

entry.name: MAV_GOTO_HOLD_AT_SPECIFIED_POSITION
entry.description: Hold at the position specified in the parameters of the DO_HOLD action

enum.name: MAV_MODE
enum.description: These defines are predefined OR-combined mode flags. There is no need to use values from this enum, but it simplifies the use of the mode flags. Note that manual input is enabled in all modes as a safety override.

entry.name: MAV_MODE_PREFLIGHT
entry.description: System is not ready to fly, booting, calibrating, etc. No flag is set.

entry.name: MAV_MODE_STABILIZE_DISARMED
entry.description: System is allowed to be active, under assisted RC control.

entry.name: MAV_MODE_STABILIZE_ARMED
entry.description: System is allowed to be active, under assisted RC control.

entry.name: MAV_MODE_MANUAL_DISARMED
entry.description: System is allowed to be active, under manual (RC) control, no stabilization

entry.name: MAV_MODE_MANUAL_ARMED
entry.description: System is allowed to be active, under manual (RC) control, no stabilization

entry.name: MAV_MODE_GUIDED_DISARMED
entry.description: System is allowed to be active, under autonomous control, manual setpoint

entry.name: MAV_MODE_GUIDED_ARMED
entry.description: System is allowed to be active, under autonomous control, manual setpoint

entry.name: MAV_MODE_AUTO_DISARMED
entry.description: System is allowed to be active, under autonomous control and navigation (the trajectory is decided onboard and not pre-programmed by waypoints)

entry.name: MAV_MODE_AUTO_ARMED
entry.description: System is allowed to be active, under autonomous control and navigation (the trajectory is decided onboard and not pre-programmed by waypoints)

entry.name: MAV_MODE_TEST_DISARMED
entry.description: UNDEFINED mode. This solely depends on the autopilot - use with caution, intended for developers only.

entry.name: MAV_MODE_TEST_ARMED
entry.description: UNDEFINED mode. This solely depends on the autopilot - use with caution, intended for developers only.

enum.name: MAV_SYS_STATUS_SENSOR
enum.description: These encode the sensors whose status is sent as part of the SYS_STATUS message.

entry.name: MAV_SYS_STATUS_PREARM_CHECK
entry.description: 0x10000000 pre-arm check status. Always healthy when armed

entry.name: MAV_SYS_STATUS_EXTENSION_USED
entry.description: 0x80000000 Extended bit-field are used for further sensor status bits (needs to be set in onboard_control_sensors_present only)

enum.name: MAV_SYS_STATUS_SENSOR_EXTENDED
enum.description: These encode the sensors whose status is sent as part of the SYS_STATUS message in the extended fields.

message.name: SYS_STATUS
message.description: The general system state. If the system is following the MAVLink standard, the system state is mainly defined by three orthogonal states/modes: The system mode, which is either LOCKED (motors shut down and locked), MANUAL (system under RC control), GUIDED (system with autonomous position control, position setpoint controlled manually) or AUTO (system guided by path/waypoint planner). The NAV_MODE defined the current flight state: LIFTOFF (often an open-loop maneuver), LANDING, WAYPOINTS or VECTOR. This represents the internal navigation state machine. The system status shows whether the system is currently active or not and if an emergency occurred. During the CRITICAL and EMERGENCY states the MAV is still considered to be active, but should start emergency procedures autonomously. After a failure occurred it should first move from active to critical to allow manual intervention and then move to emergency after a certain timeout.

message.name: SYSTEM_TIME
message.description: The system time is the time of the master clock, typically the computer clock of the main onboard computer.
message.field: Timestamp (UNIX epoch time).
Timestamp (time since system boot).

message.name: PING
message.deprecated: to be removed / merged with SYSTEM_TIME
message.description: A ping message either requesting or responding to a ping. This allows to measure the system latencies, including serial port, radio modem and UDP connections. The ping microservice is documented at https://mavlink.io/en/services/ping.html
message.field: Timestamp (UNIX Epoch time or time since system boot). The receiving end can infer timestamp format (since 1.1.1970 or since system boot) by checking for the magnitude of the number.
PING sequence
0: request ping from all receiving systems. If greater than 0: message is a ping response and number is the system id of the requesting system
0: request ping from all receiving components. If greater than 0: message is a ping response and number is the component id of the requesting component.

message.name: CHANGE_OPERATOR_CONTROL
message.field: System the GCS requests control for
0: request control of this MAV, 1: Release control of this MAV

0: key as plaintext, 1-255: future, different hashing/encryption variants. The GCS should in general use the safest mode possible initially and then gradually move down the encryption level if it gets a NACK message indicating an encryption mismatch.
Password / Key, depending on version plaintext or encrypted. 25 or less characters, NULL terminated. The characters may involve A-Z, a-z, 0-9, and "!?,.-"
